reason: Section 190.073 is a very large rural-community transition provision with distinct educational topics: content of restructuring regulations, service continuity and ministerial service provision, police-service cost phasing, and plan, boundary and by-law adjustments.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Required and optional contents of rural-community restructuring regulations
proposedGroups.reason: Subsection 190.073(1) lists what a regulation under section 190.072 may prescribe or provide, including dates, names, boundaries, first elections, services, assets and liabilities, local commissions, wards, planning instruments and transitional matters.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the matters the Lieutenant-Governor in Council may include in a rural-community incorporation, amalgamation, annexation or decrement regulation.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Continuity and ministerial provision of rural-community services
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections address continuation of existing services, liabilities after discontinuance, and ministerial provision and funding of garbage, regional-service-commission services, and animal control where the rural community has not enacted its own by-law.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain how services continue or are provided by the Minister in a rural community, including garbage, regional-service-commission services and animal control.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Ministerial police protection service and phased cost recovery
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections specifically authorize ministerial police protection service where no rural-community by-law exists and set the percentage of money the Minister may raise for 2013 through 2016 and later.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall when the Minister may provide police protection to a rural community and what cost percentages may be raised by year.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Planning, boundary, and by-law effects after rural-community restructuring
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections cover amendment or repeal of plans and boundary regulations, continuation or extension of by-laws after amalgamation, annexation and decrement, and the exclusion of a Community Planning Act subsection.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the effects of rural-community restructuring on planning regulations, boundary regulations, and existing by-laws.

reason: Section 190.074 separates corporate status and corporate powers from internal administrative structuring and expense recovery for defaults.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Rural community corporate status, territory, succession, and powers
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections make inhabitants a body corporate, include contiguous wharves and similar structures, give perpetual succession, and list corporate powers to sue, contract, charge interest, hold property and take security.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the corporate identity, territorial inclusion, succession, and legal powers of a rural community.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Rural community administrative bodies and recovery for defaulted directions
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 190.074(5) and (6) authorize creating or abolishing internal bodies and recovering expenses where a person defaults on a lawful rural-community direction.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify rural-community powers to organize administrative bodies and recover expenses when a lawful direction is not obeyed.

reason: Section 190.075 requires a corporate seal and states that contracts, deeds and other documents have no effect unless sealed and signed by the rural community mayor and clerk.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Rural community corporate seal and execution of documents
proposedGroups.reason: Section 190.075 requires a corporate seal and states that contracts, deeds and other documents have no effect unless sealed and signed by the rural community mayor and clerk.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the seal and signature requirements for rural community agreements, contracts, deeds and other documents.

reason: Section 190.076 vests rural community powers in council, assigns an advisory role on services, continues proceedings across councils, and applies election and member provisions with modifications.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Rural community council powers, continuity, elections, and member rules
proposedGroups.reason: Section 190.076 vests rural community powers in council, assigns an advisory role on services, continues proceedings across councils, and applies election and member provisions with modifications.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how rural community council exercises powers, assists the Minister, continues proceedings, and is elected or governed by applied member rules.

reason: Section 190.077 is about rural-community officers but has distinct study points for appointment authority and for eligibility, tenure and acting officers.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Appointment of rural community administrative officers
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections identify optional and mandatory rural-community offices and allow one person to hold more than one office.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall which rural-community officers council may or shall appoint and when one person may hold multiple offices.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Councillor employment limits, officer tenure, and acting officers
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections restrict appointment or employment of elected council members, exclude voluntary work, protect full-time officer tenure except auditors and specified persons, and permit acting officers.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the limits on appointing elected council members, tenure protection for officers, and use of acting officers.

reason: Section 190.078 separates duties and financial signing rules for rural-community officers from professional qualification rules for solicitors and engineers.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Duties, cheque signatures, reproduced signatures, and treasurer liability
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections address prescribed CAO and officer duties, joint cheque signing with the treasurer, reproduced signatures, and treasurer protection for by-law or resolution payments.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the duties, cheque-signing requirements, signature reproduction, and treasurer liability rule for rural community officers.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Solicitor and engineer qualification rules
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections require solicitors to be Law Society members, preserve cost recovery despite salary remuneration, and require engineers to be registered professional engineers.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify the professional qualification and cost-recovery rules for rural community solicitors and engineers.

reason: Section 190.079 covers rural-community by-law authority and the separate rules for applying broader by-law enactment, enforcement, prosecution and conflict provisions.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Rural community by-laws for services, meetings, municipal powers, and council structure
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections authorize service by-laws, require meeting-procedure by-laws, extend municipal by-law powers unless inconsistent, and allow by-laws modifying specified council composition, election, and ward matters.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the types of by-laws a rural community may or must enact for services, meetings, municipal powers and council structure.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Application and conflict rules for rural community by-laws
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 190.079(5) and (6) apply Act and regulation provisions about by-law enactment, enforcement, prosecution and penalties to rural communities, subject to a conflict rule favoring the rural-community provisions.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain how general by-law provisions apply to rural communities and what prevails if there is a conflict.

reason: Section 190.08 has one topic about administering services and entering service agreements, and another about expropriation powers and limits.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Rural community service administration, by-laws, land, and agreements
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections require the rural community to administer and pay for powers or services, authorize service by-laws, land acquisition and service-sharing agreements, natural gas agreements, and airport commission participation.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall how a rural community administers services and what agreements or land powers it may use to provide them.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Expropriation for rural community powers and service limits
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 190.08(5) and (6) authorize expropriation for powers or services but invalidate expropriation inside another rural community or municipality.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify when a rural community may expropriate and the boundary-based limit on that power.

reason: Section 190.081 is a rural-community finance provision with separable topics for annual budgets and tax rates, federal Crown assessed value, ministerial approval and revisions, and differential rates.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Annual rural community estimates, tax base amount, rate, and tax imposition
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections set the fiscal year and annual estimate resolution, including money required, amount raised on tax base, rate, real-property tax imposition, the 2010 rate rule, and other revenue sources.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall the annual estimate, tax-base, rate and revenue-source requirements for rural community finances.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Federal Crown property assessment in the rural community tax base
proposedGroups.reason: Subsections 190.081(4) and (5) state how assessed value for federal Crown property is determined for the rural community tax base.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Explain how the Minister determines assessed value for real property in a rural community owned by the Crown in right of Canada.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Ministerial approval, revisions, fixed rate, and invalidity protection
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections require revised estimates, amounts and rates if the Minister does not approve, make the approved rate the Real Property Tax Act rate, and protect that rate despite failure to pass a resolution.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Recall what happens if the Minister does not approve the estimate and when the rural community rate is fixed.

proposedGroups.titleSuggestion: Differential rural community tax rates and rate adjustment
proposedGroups.reason: These subsections permit different rates where services vary or for annexed unincorporated areas, and require adjustment so the amount to be raised stays the same.
proposedGroups.approximateLearningGoal: Identify when different rural community tax rates may be fixed and how the base rate must be adjusted.
